what_changed: Consolidation: accuracy 0.61 -> 0.82, OOD_DEV 0.31 -> 0.42, block IIA 0.48 -> 0.68, copy 0.78, pooled edit 0.35 -> 0.58, interaction 0.29 -> 0.36. Head 0 (46.5) and head 3 (25.8) write mass; each is strongly route-split (interaction 0.67 / 0.77) but the block total is only 0.36. 158 MLP neurons now match stably (identities settling).
hypothesis: (1) My step-1,200 prediction that editability would fall as the interaction grows is REFUTED here: both rose together, because the two writers' unit-specific parts partly cancel in the block. (2) The generalisation gap (ID 0.82 vs OOD_DEV 0.42) is caused mainly UPSTREAM: the layer-1 value-plus-unit binding behaves like a lookup of seen combinations, not a compositional value-rotated-by-unit-scale operation, so held-out combinations produce wrong canonical mass.
evidence: Level 2 (new read-only ood_locus tool, disclosed): canonical-mass probe at the value token 0.86 on ID vs 0.41 on OOD_DEV (block 0.62 vs 0.33); setting the block to the TRUE mass's FIT class mean raises OOD_DEV accuracy 0.42 -> 0.66 (label-using diagnostic: shows the downstream would mostly cope if mass were formed correctly); held-out mass combinations are worse (0.33) than held-out acceleration combinations (0.52).
key_question: Can the layer-1 binding be made compositional (value code rotated by unit scale) so held-out combinations form correct mass, without losing what the network already does?
best_experiment: Layer-1 compositional binding supervision: interchange the value token's and the unit token's layer-1 residuals separately with matched counterfactual targets (raw value from source with base unit; unit from source with base value), on FIT only, restricted to attn1 and the value embeddings. NOT available as a registered primitive (counterfactual supervision is defined only at the block, dims 16-63 and attn2 heads); recorded as a proposed primitive for a future registration.
intervention_rationale: The diagnosed defect lies at layer-1 token positions, which no registered primitive can target; block-level primitives act downstream of the failure (the label diagnostic shows the downstream is not the main bottleneck). Editability is high and rising, so there is no editability defect to repair either. Per the spec, a new primitive is proposed for future work rather than altering the frozen rules.
